novel_features.name: Local FTS5 search across all record types
novel_features.description: Full-text search across every synced object's records in one command. Returns typed hits across company, person, opportunity, and every mirrored Salesforce object.
novel_features.rationale: The Unify Data API has no LIST or SEARCH endpoint for records. Search only exists if you build it from a local mirror.
novel_features.why_it_matters: When you need to answer 'is this domain in our workspace anywhere?' across Unify and Salesforce-mirrored objects, this is the one command. No N find-unique calls.
novel_features.group: Local read layer over a write-only API

novel_features.name: Read-only SQL over the local mirror
novel_features.description: Run read-only SQL queries with joins across per-object record tables. Cross Unify standard objects with Salesforce-mirrored ones in a single query.
novel_features.rationale: The API has no query/filter surface for records. SQL is the missing read layer.
novel_features.example: unify-pp-cli sql "SELECT json_extract(attrs,'$.name') as name, json_extract(attrs,'$.employee_count') as employees FROM record_company WHERE json_extract(attrs,'$.industry')='Retail' AND CAST(json_extract(attrs,'$.employee_count') AS INTEGER) >= 200" --agent
novel_features.why_it_matters: Answers operational questions the API can't: industry/segment slices, employee thresholds, joined opportunity/owner views. The query mode an agent reaches for instead of writing scratch Python.
novel_features.group: Local read layer over a write-only API

novel_features.name: Coverage report between two object tables
novel_features.description: Set-difference report between two record tables on a shared key with optional bucketing by attribute and matched-but-stale rows.
novel_features.rationale: Coverage is a join + set-diff problem; the API exposes neither operation. Only computable locally.
novel_features.example: unify-pp-cli coverage --left salesforce_account --right company --key domain --by industry --agent
novel_features.why_it_matters: Tells you which Salesforce accounts are missing from Unify (and vice versa), bucketed by industry/owner — the central artifact of an account-coverage review.

novel_features.name: Score-divergence audit
novel_features.description: Flag records where two numeric attributes diverge beyond a threshold. Powers scoring sanity checks across Unify-internal and Salesforce-mirrored score fields.
novel_features.rationale: Pure local SQL; the API doesn't expose comparisons across attributes.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Catches the 'false-scoring auto-deduct-50pts' class of bugs before they ship into a campaign.

novel_features.name: Schema snapshot + diff
novel_features.description: Snapshot objects, attributes, and attribute options; diff two snapshots to find adds, removes, and type changes.
novel_features.rationale: Unify has no server-side schema-change audit log.
novel_features.why_it_matters: When the SF-aligned admin adds new fields, you can prove what changed between any two points in time and act on the delta.

novel_features.name: Batch domain vetting
novel_features.description: Read a CSV column of match values, run find-unique in parallel for each, and enrich each row with exists/has_opportunity/owner/last_activity_at.
novel_features.rationale: find-unique is per-key only; batch vetting is exactly the workflow the no-list constraint makes impossible without orchestration.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pre-launch vet for an outbound sequence drops from N alt-tabs to one command. Bulk pre-flight without bothering an engineer.

novel_features.name: CSV upsert plan preview
novel_features.description: Predict what an upsert from CSV will do (create / update / no-op counts per row) by combining the local mirror with find-unique fallbacks.
novel_features.rationale: Upsert has 6 merge modes; a dry-run plan from the API alone can't tell you which existing records will change.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Stops you from running a 2k-row upsert blind. Reports per-row outcome with a writable plan you can pipe back into upsert.

novel_features.name: Local reference trace
novel_features.description: Walk reference attributes (opportunities, people, owner) from a starting record without N+1 API calls.
novel_features.rationale: Reference cardinality is in the schema; the API forces per-record GETs to follow refs. Local mirror traversal is the optimization.
novel_features.why_it_matters: One-shot 'show me everything connected to this company' for spot-checks and pre-call prep.
novel_features.group: Local read layer over a write-only API

novel_features.name: Watchlist-driven sync
novel_features.description: Persist match-keys for records you care about; sync refreshes them via parallel find-unique on every run.
novel_features.rationale: No list endpoint exists, so sync needs an explicit ID list. The watchlist is the cold-start solution.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Without a watchlist, sync has nothing to enumerate. With it, your daily refresh hits the records you actually use.
novel_features.group: Local read layer over a write-only API

narrative.headline: The read layer Unify's API doesn't ship. Local search, SQL, and coverage reports over a CRM that has no list-records endpoint.
narrative.value_prop: Unify's Data API gives you upsert, find-unique, and write — but no way to list, search, or query records. This CLI ships the missing read layer: local SQLite mirror with FTS5 search, read-only SQL across Unify and Salesforce-mirrored objects, schema snapshot/diff, coverage and score-divergence audits, batch CSV vetting, and dry-run-by-default upserts.
narrative.auth_narrative: Set UNIFY_API_KEY (generated at Settings → Developers in the Unify dashboard) to a Data API key. The CLI uses the same X-Api-Key header as the official Python and TypeScript SDKs.

quickstart.comment: Inventory every object in your workspace (Unify standard + Salesforce-mirrored)
Tell sync which records to track — records have no list endpoint, so this is the cursor
Mirror schema + watched records into the local SQLite store
FTS5 across every synced record type — the read layer the API doesn't ship

quickstart.command: unify-pp-cli sql "SELECT id, json_extract(attrs,'$.name') as name FROM record_company WHERE json_extract(attrs,'$.industry')='Retail' LIMIT 10" --agent
quickstart.comment: Joinable SQL over the local mirror — answers the questions the API can't

troubleshoots.fix: Re-issue your key at Settings → Developers in Unify and re-export UNIFY_API_KEY; the CLI sends X-Api-Key on every call.

troubleshoots.symptom: search/sql returns 0 rows but the record exists in Unify
troubleshoots.fix: The record isn't in the local mirror yet. Run unify-pp-cli watch add <object> --match <key>=<value>, then unify-pp-cli sync.
Confirm the attribute you're matching on is a unique attribute (find-unique requires it). Run unify-pp-cli attrs list <object> to inspect.

troubleshoots.symptom: upsert says it would create when you expected an update
troubleshoots.fix: Pass --plan first: it shows per-row creates vs updates vs no-ops without writing. Adjust --match-on or merge mode and re-run.
You need at least two snapshots. Run unify-pp-cli schema snapshot today and again later, then diff between them.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI any time you need to read, search, or audit Unify Data API records — the official API and SDKs can write and find-unique but cannot list, search, or join. Reach for it for account-coverage reviews against Salesforce, scoring audits, schema-change tracking, batch domain vetting before outbound sequencing, and dry-run-by-default CSV upserts. Not the right tool for live event streaming or the Intent API (browser pixel) — only the Data API surface.

recipes.title: Pre-launch vet a sequence target list
recipes.explanation: For each domain, parallel find-unique + local enrichment; outputs one row per input with exists/has_opportunity/owner.

recipes.title: Find every retail company with >=200 employees and a recent opportunity
recipes.command: unify-pp-cli sql "SELECT json_extract(c.attrs,'$.name') as name, json_extract(c.attrs,'$.domain') as domain FROM record_company c JOIN record_opportunity o ON json_extract(o.attrs,'$.company_id') = c.id WHERE json_extract(c.attrs,'$.industry')='Retail' AND o.created_at > date('now','-30 days')" --agent --select rows
recipes.explanation: The query Nate writes scratch Python for today — one SQL, narrowed JSON output for the agent.

recipes.title: Account coverage against Salesforce, bucketed by industry
recipes.command: unify-pp-cli coverage --left salesforce_account --right company --key domain --by industry --agent
recipes.explanation: Set-diff per industry bucket: which SF accounts are missing in Unify, which Unify companies have no SF counterpart, which are stale.

recipes.title: What schema fields did Emily add this week?
recipes.explanation: Snapshot today, then diff against last Friday's snapshot. Output the per-object adds/removes/type-changes only — the noisy fields you don't care about are filtered.

recipes.title: Dry-run a 2k-row CSV upsert before writing
recipes.explanation: Predicts per-row creates vs updates vs no-ops by combining the local mirror with find-unique fallbacks. Run it twice; only the second --execute writes.
